text: DSH Diagnostic Tutor 是面向 DeepSeek Harness Web 客户端的诊断式学习运行时。它通过 DSH 工具保存学习目标、诊断地图、课程路径、结构化课程内容和复习状态，并在 Web 界面提供学习地图、课程与当前课程面板。用户可以从自己的学习目标开始，逐步记录诊断证据，查看课程路径和学习内容，安排待办并复习卡片。适合希望在 DSH 对话旁持续查看学习进度、管理个人课程状态的学习者。安装后由 DSH 的工具和存储服务提供运行基础。

DSH Diagnostic Tutor is a diagnosis-first learning runtime for the DeepSeek Harness web client. It stores learning goals, diagnosis maps, course paths, lessons, and review state, with a web UI for viewing maps, studying lessons, managing tasks, and reviewing cards.

DSH Diagnostic Tutor 的功能「学习目标与诊断地图」：创建学习目标并读取或更新对应的诊断地图，记录学习节点和证据。通过模型可调用的目标与地图工具完成输入和变更。
DSH Diagnostic Tutor 的功能「课程路径与学习内容」：读取课程路径、更新路径及会话课程运行状态，并保存结构化课程内容供学习界面呈现。
DSH Diagnostic Tutor 的功能「个人学习资料」：把粘贴文本或单个本地 Markdown、文本文件加入个人资料库，再读取选定资料以支持课程引用。
DSH Diagnostic Tutor 的功能「学习计划」：读取 Today 待办，并新增、完成或移除任务；界面显示近期任务和可用的日历导出入口。
DSH Diagnostic Tutor 的功能「间隔复习」：添加复习卡片、列出到期卡片并记录 again、hard、good 或 easy 评级以安排下次复习。

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Universal Diagnostic Tutor for DeepSeek Harness：> **From a Tutor Skill to a Learning Runtime.**

Diagnosis-first AI learning runtime for DeepSeek Harness — map what you need,
learn interactively, and move to the next best step.

<sub>The learning surface docked in the right sidebar, beside the conversation. The map, the lesson and the chat are on screen at once, so answering a check never means leaving the lesson.</sub>

**Today → Course → Study**, with Review, Knowledge & evidence and Insights as

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Status：- **Today**: one next action, due review, deadline, today's plan and your courses.
- **Course**: the accepted route, module/lesson list, one continue action; when no
  route is accepted, a three-step **Goal → Diagnosis → Course preview** flow.
- **Study**: one stored lesson block at a time, with a single primary action.
  Quiz and flashcard answers still go through the runtime; nothing is graded or

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Status：The content/input/review loop remains: typeset math, formula/code/quiz/flashcard/
resource/comparison blocks, plus interactive slider, step-through and safe inline SVG
figures, sources with citations, Today/ICS, spaced review with undo, and read-only
Insights.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Status：`0.4.0` adds the reference visual system, explicit **half / main / full-screen**
Study modes, a lesson step rail, text/Markdown learner materials with citation-aware
prompt context, and the first production interactive blocks. It targets the current
desktop runtime **DSH 0.2.2-rc.1**.

`0.4.1` completes the reference UI with the **Library / welcome** state: compact

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Status：Install it with
`dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-diagnostic-tutor@0.4.1` — no clone, no
`pnpm install`, no build step. A checkout can be installed instead (see
[Installing a checkout](#installing-a-checkout-instead-of-the-package)).

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Status：It is still early. The [limitations](#known-limitations) are listed rather than
left to be discovered: no PDF extraction, no RAG, no automatic external resource
fetching, no analytics. Review scheduling is a local interval heuristic, not
FSRS. Course routes are proposed by the teaching model, never generated by the
runtime, and a route never marks knowledge as mastered.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Two halves, one system：The unusual thing about this project is that **the teaching and the runtime are
separate programs**, and only one of them makes decisions.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Two halves, one system：| | Owns | Where | | --- | --- | --- | | **[Universal Diagnostic Tutor](https://github.com/SenmuuuuW/universal-diagnostic-tutor-skill) skill**
= **the teaching brain** | What to teach next: diagnosis, teaching moves, pacing, when a check is passed, what the next step is | that repository (v2.1, MIT) | | **`dsh-diagnostic-tutor`**
= **the learning runtime** | Where it is kept: persistent learner state, the diagnosis map, structured lessons, the UI | here |

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Two halves, one system：That split is not a packaging detail. This repository contains **no teaching
logic**: no rule that says "if blocked, explain the prerequisite", no rule that
says "if wrong, give a simpler example". Those live in the skill. The runtime
stores what the tutor decided, shows it, and never decides it.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · The loop：```
Goal  →  Diagnose  →  Map  →  Learn  →  Check  →  Decide  →  Next lesson
 │                      │        │         │         │            │
 │                      │        │         │         │            └ the tutor names
 │                      │        │         │         │              the next node, with a reason

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · The loop：Read left to right, that is also the guarantee: **the runtime never advances on
its own.** A decision is stored with the tutor's reason, shown to the learner,
and waits to be pressed.

with the real skill:

| --- | --- |
|  | **First use.** No goal yet. One question, and the sentence that answers it — no wizard, no empty dashboard. |
|  | **The diagnosis map.** Six nodes, each traceable to evidence, nested by depth. `blocked` and `checked` read at a glance; nothing is `confirmed` without a check behind it. |

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Why this is not just another AI tutor：Most "AI tutor" projects are a prompt wrapped around a chat box: the model
teaches, and nothing about the learner survives the conversation. Three things
are different here.

**The teaching brain is a real, separate artifact.** Diagnosis, teaching moves,
pacing and mastery judgement live in a written skill with its own protocols —
not in a system prompt this repository invented. This plugin depends on it and
refuses to duplicate it.
section: Why this is not just another AI tutor

text:
dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Why this is not just another AI tutor：**State is real, and it is the learner's.** A goal, a map of what you actually
know, and a record of the evidence behind each status. Nothing is `confirmed`
without a check to back it, nothing is scored, and it is all visible and
exportable.

**The runtime does not decide.** The tutor names the next step and says why; the
runtime stores that and shows it; the learner presses Continue. There is no
path by which progress advances on its own.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Why this is not just another AI tutor：Its state vocabulary is not invented here either: nodes carry the skill's own
seven status terms, and checks carry its six readiness outcomes.

text:
dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Why a map does not contradict diagnosis-first：The skill is explicit that a broad goal must **never** become a pre-expanded
curriculum or a course outline. This plugin does not produce one. Nodes appear
only as diagnosis reveals them, every node is `unconfirmed` until a check
produces evidence, and the map is reversible — new evidence moves it. What you
see is a *diagnosis map*, not a syllabus.

text:
dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Known limitations：**Math is rendered as MathML on the host.** The tutor writes LaTeX by convention
— `\(...\)` inline, `\[...\]` display — and the host pre-renders it with
KaTeX's MathML output before storing the block. The browser renders native
MathML through a tag/attribute whitelist; no font or CSS is fetched. Invalid
TeX inside a text block falls back to the old styled source; an invalid
`formula` block is refused at write time. Browser MathML quality varies, and
this build ships no KaTeX CSS/fonts.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Known limitations：**Skill presence requires a live Agent.** The runtime checks the open
conversation's Agent scope on each overview, including its workspace. Before an
Agent exists, or while discovery is empty or incomplete, it reports `cannot tell`
and the panel stays quiet. Polling picks up later registration and Agent changes.
If lessons never appear, check the skill first.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Known limitations：**Storage is one document.** Every record lives in
`<dsh-home>/storages/udt.json`. It is readable, copyable and easy to export, and
it is also a single point of failure: a record that no longer matches its schema
stops the plugin from loading. Nothing is deleted when that happens, the error
names the table and the key, and removing the record by hand restores the rest —
but **export before you edit it**.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Known limitations：**The tutor does not always converge.** It can judge `more-practice` on the same
node several turns running, each time writing a fresh check. That is its pacing
rather than the runtime's, but it decides whether a node ever finishes and the
loop moves on.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Compatibility：A DSH profile can resolve **more than one harness version at once** (the running
host, the shared profile fallback, and each plugin's own store). Treat this
matrix as load-bearing, not decoration.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Compatibility：**2026-11-04 追加 `0.2.2-rc.1`（当前桌面 runtime）验证**：devDependencies 升到 DSH `0.2.2-rc.1`、cordis `4.1.0`、schemastery `3.19.0`；隔离 `DSH_HOME` 中安装本仓库插件后，`/overview`、`/diagnostics`、`/plan/ics`、`/review` 均 200，domain `udt` v1、`issues: []`；真实浏览器加载 Learning map 与 Learn 侧栏无 Runtime exception；`tsc`、677 tests、build、31 browser cases 通过。`0.2.2` 的 `AgentRegistry` 新增 `sessionProjections` inject，测试 harness 补了最小服务；生产源码的 API 使用无需改动。

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Compatibility：**2026-10-30 追加 `0.2.1-rc.5`（当前桌面 runtime）验证**：隔离 profile 加载 `0.2.0` 插件无异常，tsc 与 639 tests 在 rc5 类型/依赖下通过，真实数据副本的 Learning map / 知识与证据 / 复习 / 洞察 UI 无客户端异常；没有发现需要改插件代码的 API 破坏。

Phase 1–6 的本机 boot 矩阵（2026-10-29）覆盖 `0.2.1-rc.3`、`0.2.1-rc.2`、`0.2.0-rc.2`、`0.1.7-alpha.2` 的插件加载、本地路由、domain v1 与客户端启动；其中 rc3/alpha.2 还通过了 tarball 安装，并用真实模型完成 lesson → Review 评分/撤销 → Insights；rc2/rc20 的完整真实会话仍是补充项。详见 [`docs/planning/COMPATIBILITY.md`](docs/planning/COMPATIBILITY.md)。

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Compatibility：- **Named exports only.** A `export default` plugin makes Cordis' loader prefer
  `.default` and **silently drop `inject`** — a documented DSH outage. Pinned by
  a test that fails if a default export is ever introduced.
- **`@deepseek-ai/*` is imported `type`-only**, so the compiler erases it and no
  second runtime copy can be resolved. Enforced by `verbatimModuleSyntax`, and
  verified on the built artifact (it contains zero imports).
- **No `instanceof` across package boundaries.** Take runtime objects from `ctx`.
- Peer ranges name the release lines this plugin was verified on. DSH ships
  prereleases, and npm's semver only admits a prerelease when its line is named
  in the range — so the compatibility matrix above, not the range floor, is the
  contract. Dev dependencies pin one exact cohort for the type baseline.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · UI baseline for redesign：The current surfaces, state model and screenshots (generated from fixtures) live in
[`docs/design/ui-baseline/index.html`](docs/design/ui-baseline/index.html) with a
detailed handoff in
[`docs/design/ui-baseline/README.md`](docs/design/ui-baseline/README.md). It covers
the system structure, Learning map / Current lesson surfaces, every route-page state
and the design constraints a new UI must keep.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Diagnostics：Monitoring is local and content-free: no chat, goal, lesson or evidence text is
recorded, and nothing is sent anywhere.

```sh
pnpm doctor                 # human-readable health report
node scripts/doctor.mjs --json   # machine-readable
node scripts/doctor.mjs --strict # exit 1 if an error-severity issue exists
```

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Diagnostics：It reads `<dsh-home>/storages/udt.json` plus the event journal and reports each
project's stage, pending/failed tutor requests (with age), stalled attempts and
route-length conflicts. The same report is available at
`GET /diagnostic-tutor/api/diagnostics` (loopback-only, like every plugin
route).

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Diagnostics：The host journal lives at `<dsh-home>/logs/diagnostic-tutor-events.jsonl`
(`DSH_DIAGNOSTIC_TUTOR_EVENTS` overrides the path, `off` disables it). It logs
lifecycle events only: tool names and operations, durations, request outcomes,
provider error messages (truncated). A single file is capped at 1 MB and
rotated once.

text:
dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Learner state and the diagnosis map：Courses, maps, lessons and evidence are shared by the learner's conversations.
Project selection, focus, next step and handoff belong to one conversation,
identified by its session ID. The legacy `activeCourseId` remains in storage for
compatibility; it does not select a project for a conversation. A fresh
conversation starts with the library, even when historical projects exist.
section: Learner state and the diagnosis map

text:
dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Learner state and the diagnosis map：| Conversation selection | Project binding |
| --- | --- |
| `none` | A new goal, or a validated write explicitly naming a course or node in this conversation, may select its project. Reading shared data does not select it. |
| `new` | The learner pressed **Start something new**. Only a new goal created here may bind; historical map or lesson writes leave this choice intact. |
| `project` | The selected course is the default for tools. Creating another goal does not replace it; writes to another course require selecting that course first. |
section: Learner state and the diagnosis map

text:
dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Learner state and the diagnosis map：`udt_status` reports this conversation's `selection` and, only for `project`,
its `courseId`. Goal, map and lesson writes return `projectAdopted` and
`projectBinding`: `adopted`, `already-selected`, `not-selected`, or
`missing-session-id`. A choice made while a write is pending takes precedence
over that write's adoption. Without a reliable session ID, status reports
`sessionAvailable: false`; explicit shared writes can still be stored, but their
result is `missing-session-id` and they claim no conversation binding.
section: Learner state and the diagnosis map

text:
dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Learner state and the diagnosis map：Two deliberate rules:

- **zod is the contract.** Every record is validated at the durable boundary, so
  a hand-edited or corrupt document fails loudly instead of entering memory.
- **No scores, ever.** There is no field for points, grades or percentages —
  the skill forbids turning mastery into a score, and a test asserts that no
  such key exists anywhere in the persisted document.
section: Learner state and the diagnosis map

text:
dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Learner state and the diagnosis map：Records are never mutated in place; writes go through `put`/`set` on one
per-domain write chain, so concurrent writers cannot interleave.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Tools：The division is the architecture: the tutor decides **what** to teach, when to
check, and what an answer showed; the runtime decides **what may be stored** and
renders it. There is no branch anywhere in this repository that says "if blocked
then explain the prerequisite" — that is the skill's call, made in the chat.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · The loop：```
press Start learning
   → focus recorded (courseId, nodeId, startedAt, status)
   → the tutor is woken in that conversation with the node named
   → the tutor teaches into the surface via udt_lesson_update

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · The decision：`action` is the skill's six readiness outcomes, reused rather than re-invented:
the words for "what this concept showed" and "where that sends the learner" are
the same words. The runtime only needs one structural fact about each — whether
it names a target:

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · The decision：| outcome | target | means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `advance` / `advance-with-caution` | required | move there |
| `step-down` | required | the blocker; usually a prerequisite |
| `review-first` | optional | go back, or review here |
| `more-practice` / `diagnose-again` | forbidden | stay here |

A move ends the focus and stamps `endedAt`; staying leaves it open. Nothing
moves on its own — the learner reads the reason and presses Continue.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · The wait, measured：Moving to a node is not instant, so the wait is a **persisted record** keyed by
target node — which makes it idempotent, refresh-proof, restart-proof and
retryable — and it carries a timestamp per stage:

```
requestedAt → focusRecordedAt → promptedAt → firstActivityAt → lessonAt → observedAt
```

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · The wait, measured：The same record is the progress line (`focus recorded` → `tutor requested` →
`tutor working` → `lesson ready`, with elapsed seconds) and the measurement. A
real run against DSH 0.1.6-alpha.2 and the real skill:

| stage | when |
| --- | --- |
| focus persisted | 0.0s |
| followup accepted | 0.0s |
| first tutor activity | 1.0s |
| lesson written | 26.1s |
| UI observed | 26.1s |

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · The wait, measured：**The plugin costs about a second; the rest is the model writing.** A stall is
derived from the record rather than stored, and retrying never touches the
focus — a timeout is a statement about the wait, not about where the learner is.

`Start learning` is a **user-role turn attributed to this plugin**, not injected
context: `agent.inject()` would add model-visible context without waking an idle
agent, so nothing would happen until the learner typed. Opening a turn is what
the button means.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Two surfaces, one state：| Surface | Where | For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Learning map** | the main column (`main`, key `diagnostic-tutor-map`) | browsing — course route, every lesson Overview, knowledge & evidence |
| **Current lesson** | the right sidebar tab, beside the chat | the lesson itself — teaching units, and checks answered in the chat |

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Two surfaces, one state：One page for browsing, one surface for learning. The page never starts a lesson;
the tab never decides what to teach. Both read the same `useLearning` state and
the same path client, so they cannot disagree about what is focused, accepted or
written. **Open current lesson** on the map returns to the conversation with the
lesson tab open in the same step.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Two surfaces, one state：The container for the main column is the map page. A full-page lesson panel used
to exist as a second main destination; it was removed so the same lesson is not
offered in two places. The standalone full-page component is still used by the
preview and the tests, but the plugin does not register it.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Teaching-brain detection：Each overview asks the platform's own Agent and Skill registries whether the
Universal Diagnostic Tutor skill is available in the requesting session's live
Agent scope and cwd. No path is hardcoded, no skill root is assumed, and nothing
is copied. Missing services and incomplete discovery return an inconclusive
status; complete scoped discovery can establish presence or absence.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Teaching-brain detection：Compatibility is probed by **capability**, not by a version string: the skill's
maintenance contract permits only `name` and `description` in frontmatter, so
it cannot declare a version. The result carries a short content digest as a
version hint.

Paths, fingerprints and compatibility details stay **internal**, absent from
every tool output and overview. The overview exposes only availability. The skill
forbids naming its files, versions or repository in learner-facing text.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · How the two halves agree：The skill's guardrails say mastery tracking must never become "scores,
databases, hidden memory, or a curriculum roadmap", while this runtime
deliberately persists state and renders a map.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · How the two halves agree：Until `v0.0.8` that tension was bridged from this side: a short system-prompt
section explained the runtime's storage semantics to the teaching brain. UDT
v2.1's `learning_runtime_contract.md` now states all of it in the skill's own
words — what a runtime may hold, when a decision is recorded, and that a turn
which judged an answer is *not finished* until the next step is recorded — so
the bridge was **deleted rather than kept as a second voice**. The plugin got
better at it, which is the evidence it belonged upstream.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · The page and the lesson surface：The browser half registers three things: the **Learning map** icon in the
sidebar (`sidebar.panellist`, a `list`), the page it opens (`main`, a `keyed`
slot, key `diagnostic-tutor-map`), and the **Current lesson** tab in the right
sidebar (a tab type plus its body and title). The map's sidebar `id` and its
`main` key come from one constant — a drift between them would leave the icon
opening nothing.

text:
dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · The page and the lesson surface：The route tab shows one stage at a time and one next step. A progress bar names
the four stages — goal & time, initial diagnosis, route, learning — and a
**Next step** card always answers "what now?" with a single primary action
(set the goal, request or answer the diagnosis, request the route, accept the
version, start the first lesson, continue the current one) plus at most one
real alternative. Competing action rows live in the folded history, not beside
it. Before a goal is saved the wizard owns the page; while the tutor is asking
diagnostic questions the card points back to the conversation, shows how long it
has waited, says whether the tutor is still thinking, and on a failed turn
retries with the current model and opens the chat (the failure is recorded on
the path request, so it survives a restart; provider errors are translated into
billing / auth / rate-limit / network / context advice); route versions
appear only after the diagnosis is complete or skipped; once accepted, the page
leads with the route canvas. A proposed or accepted route shows its total study
time, the weeks it takes at the saved weekly budget

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · The page and the lesson surface：Entering learning follows the conversation, not the window. A project is
shared, but its focus and planned runs belong to a conversation, so the project
library and **Open current lesson** ask the host which conversation was last
learning the project (`GET /project/session`, read-only) and switch there with

text:
dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Learning Blocks：A block is `{ id, type, content, metadata? }`. The **schema is host-side**
(zod-validated at the durable boundary) and the **renderers are browser-side**,
keyed by `type`:

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Learning Blocks：| Type | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `text` | `md` — markdown, plus host `math[]` fragments for typeset formulas |
| `example` | `title`, `steps[]`, `takeaway?` |
| `diagram` | `format` (`ascii` \| `mermaid`), `spec`, `caption?` |
| `check` | `prompt`, `expect?`, `hint?` — the stop-and-wait surface |
| `formula` | `tex`, `display?`, host-rendered `mathml`, `caption?` |
| `code` | `language?`, `source`, `caption?` — displayed, never executed |
| `quiz` | `title?`, `questions[]` (`mcq`/`short`); answers are recorded, never graded by the runtime |
| `flashcard` | `front`, `back`, `tags?`; self-report is recorded, not scheduled as mastery |
| `resource` | `title`, optional `sourceId`/`locator`/`url`/`note` |
| `comparison` | `columns[]`, `rows[][]`, `caption?` |
| `slider` | safe expression in `x`, `min`/`max`/`step`/`initial`, optional `title`, `prompt`, `unit`, `caption` |
| `step-through` | `frames[{title?, body}]`; learner-paced sequence with previous/next |
| `figure` | `alt`, inline `svg`, optional `title`, `caption`, `animation`; sanitized SVG only |

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Learning Blocks：Blocks may also carry `sourceRefs: [{sourceId, locator}]`; every reference is
checked against the `sources` table at write time. The stored schema accepts an
**unknown type** from a newer host and the client renders a readable placeholder;
the current model tool still writes only known types.
The Learning map also shows a compact **Today** card when `udt_plan_update` has created open plan items, with a done action and an **Export calendar** action for dated items. DSH's own `schedule` is session-local, so this is an explicit calendar export rather than a push notification. Review cards and their local interval scheduler are stored but have no separate review surface yet.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Browser API：The browser's core calls, at `/diagnostic-tutor/api` (the full route list is in
[the architecture notes](docs/planning/CURRENT-ARCHITECTURE.md)):

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Browser API：| Route | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /overview` | the current course and its whole map (`course: null` on a first run) |
| `GET /node?id=` | one node with its evidence, parent and children |
| `GET /project/session?courseId=` | the conversation that should resume a project (read-only) |
| `POST /lesson {nodeId}` | the prototype lesson, built once and reused after that |
| `GET /source?id=` | one stored source and its text, for a citation preview |
| `POST /path/answer` | record a quiz/flashcard submission on the active attempt |
| `GET /plan/ics` | download open, dated Today plan items as an ICS calendar |
| `GET /review` | due review cards (read-only) |
| `POST /review/grade` | record a review rating and reschedule |
| `POST /review/undo` | restore the previous schedule after the latest grade |
| `GET /insights?courseId=` | read-only course insight counts |
| `POST /plan/task` | mark a Today plan item done (learner action; plan only) |

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Browser API：Every request passes a **trust fence**: a bare `ctx.webServer.register()` route
inherits no authentication, so the route checks that the request arrived at a
loopback `Host`, from a loopback `Origin`, and is not marked cross-site. Anything
else gets `403` and no body. The browser receives **views only** — no storage
path, no domain handle, no raw record.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Interface language：Every plugin surface ships copy in **English and Simplified Chinese**: the
Learning map page, the course route, the docked Current-lesson tab, the
standalone full-page panel used by the preview and tests, and the shared
next-step card, handoff line and welcome row. The sidebar Learn action and its
missing-conversation explanation switch too. A toggle in the map header (and in
the lesson surfaces) changes the copy in place; the language is saved on the
learner profile (`preferredLanguage`, via `GET /preferences` and
`POST /preferences/language`), so it survives a restart and applies to every
conversation. The choice applies immediately and is saved in the background: a
failed request keeps the local choice rather than flipping the UI back.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Interface language：It is copy, not content: the tutor's teaching, the learner's goal text, lesson
overviews, node titles and recorded evidence are never machine-translated, and
the model is not instructed to change language by the toggle. Three things stay
outside the switch: the **Learning map** sidebar label (registered once when the
plugin loads, so it cannot follow an in-place change), server/model error text
and dynamic handoff details as generated, and the development preview's own
toolbar.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Preview：The panel takes its API as a prop, so the UI runs with no DSH and no agent:

```sh
pnpm build && pnpm preview     # then open the printed URL
```

`preview/index.html` loads the **real built bundle** through a
`__ModuleLoader__` shim over `preview/fixture.js`, which models a learner who
said "I want to learn machine learning" with shaky maths:

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Preview：```
Machine Learning            [goal, unconfirmed]
├─ Math Foundations         [prerequisite, blocked]
│  ├─ Linear Algebra        [part-of, unconfirmed]
│  ├─ Calculus              [part-of, unconfirmed]

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Preview：Two query parameters reach the states that are otherwise awkward to produce on
demand — `?scenario=` (`first-use`, `map`, `handoff`, `next`, `stay`, `noskill`,
`long`, `scroll`, `library`, `new`, `showcase`, `curriculum`, `path-draft`,
`path-setup`, `path-assessment`) and `?surface=tab` / `?surface=map` for the
docked right-sidebar tab and the standalone map page. The scenario switch is in
the page's toolbar, and the theme toggle sets the same
`body[data-ds-dark-theme]` attribute DSH does. The page carries the real DSH
design tokens for the same reason: with hardcoded fallbacks in their place, a
token that resolves to near-white in dark mode looks perfectly fine locally.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Preview：To capture the panel from a *live* profile instead:

```sh
pnpm screenshot "<dsh-url-with-token>" preview/dsh-ui.png
```

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Auditing the presentation：```sh
pnpm preview                                                     # in one shell
pnpm audit:ui http://127.0.0.1:8391/?scenario=next                # in another
pnpm audit:ui "<dsh-url-with-token>" /tmp/audit --surface=tab
pnpm check:scroll http://127.0.0.1:8391/ /tmp/udt-scroll-check

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Auditing the presentation：The scroll regression requires local Chrome and runs against the built bundle.
The preview uses a clipped, fixed-height slot like DSH, so the whole document
cannot scroll to mask an unscrollable plugin. The check sends real wheel events
and verifies bottom content remains visible in the tab, expanded tab, stacked
panel, all three wide-panel panes, and long library/welcome views, in both themes.
Only fixture data is used; no live learner state is changed. The ordinary visual
audit alone does **not** verify scrolling.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Auditing the presentation：The visual audit measures, at each width this project targets and in both themes: the contrast
of every control's own text against its own fill, class names in the DOM that no
rule matches, how many controls carry primary weight in one view, tap targets
under 28px, type under 10.5px, and anything spilling or clipped. It prints a
table, writes `findings.json`, and saves screenshots — it does not fail the run,
so a human can disagree with it.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Auditing the presentation：That is not a substitute for looking. It is what makes looking affordable: the
docked tab's invisible primary button and the dark-mode 1.05:1 controls were
both found by it, in a live profile, in seconds.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · a relative path would resolve against the profile, not your checkout.：`tests/harness.ts` mounts the **same storage stack the standard profiles use**
(`systemPrompt` → `tools`, and `storage` → `storage-json` → `storage-domain`)

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Without the teaching brain：Install the plugin without the skill and nothing breaks: the plugin loads, the
panel opens, the map and the lesson surface render, and `GET /export` and
`POST /reset` work. What does not happen is teaching — nothing writes a lesson,
because nothing is making teaching decisions.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Without the teaching brain：**Availability is checked for the conversation you have open.** On every
`GET /overview?sessionId=…`, the plugin resolves that session's live Agent from
DSH's Agent registry and asks the Skill registry for a complete snapshot using
`{ scope: agent, cwd: agent.session.header.cwd }`. A root catalog containing
Office skills cannot establish whether that Agent has a tutor. Services are
resolved for each request, so delayed registration, removal and preset changes
are picked up by the panel's existing polling. The runtime reports three states:

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Without the teaching brain：| `teachingBrain` | meaning | what the panel does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `true` | found and model-invocable in the live Agent scope | nothing |
| `false` | unavailable after complete scoped discovery with entries | says a tutor is needed |
| `null` | no live Agent, empty/incomplete discovery, or unsupported/unavailable service | says nothing |

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Without the teaching brain：An earlier revision treated "not in my catalog" as "not installed" and showed a
notice on that basis. In a web profile that was a confident, wrong answer — the
notice would have appeared with the skill installed and in use. It only fires on
`false` now.

The lesson in the meantime is the honest one: if lessons never appear, check
that the skill is installed for your agent before suspecting the runtime.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Where your data lives, and what happens when it breaks：Everything is stored **locally**, in one JSON document:
`<dsh-home>/storages/udt.json`. Nothing is sent anywhere, there is no account,
and the file is plain enough to read.

**Export before you edit it.** Hand-editing is not blocked, but every record is
validated against its schema when the store opens, so one record that no longer
matches stops the plugin from loading.
section: Where your data lives, and what happens when it breaks

text:
dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Where your data lives, and what happens when it breaks：**What is true today.** A damaged record fails the open, is reported with the
table and key that failed, and is **not deleted**. The plugin loads inert rather
than failing the rest of the profile, and removing the offending record restores
everything else. `GET /export` on a healthy store is the way to make sure you
still have your data.
section: Where your data lives, and what happens when it breaks

text:
dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Where your data lives, and what happens when it breaks：**What is not true, and is not claimed.** The platform has a record-recovery
option, `invalidRecords: 'backup-and-skip'`, which moves a bad record aside and
opens without it. This plugin **does not declare it**, because under the
`single` layout the platform would ignore it: the option only runs when the
store can move a *per-record* document aside, and here one document holds
everything. Declaring it would read like a recovery guarantee while doing
nothing, which is worse than not having it. So a bad record is **not** backed
up and skipped, and this README says so rather than implying a recovery ability
that does not run.
section: Where your data lives, and what happens when it breaks

text:
dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Storage architecture is frozen for v0.1.0：Decided, and not revisited before the first release: `single` layout, no
per-record, no id migration. The recovery strategy is the one described above —
precise errors, nothing destroyed, export/reset, hand repair.
section: Storage architecture is frozen for v0.1.0

text:
dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Why not `per-record`：Switching the layout would make that option live, so it was tested against the
platform rather than assumed. Migration is fine: a real store's 1 course,
6 nodes, 3 lessons, 1 focus and 2 decisions were all seeded into per-record
documents, with the original file left untouched.

Writing is not. In `per-record`, each record key becomes a path segment and must
match `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+`:

```
unit 'udt': per-record key '机器学习' is not path-safe (must match /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/)
```

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Why not `per-record`：The `:` alone is enough — `ml:math` is rejected too. Every node, lesson and
decision id in this plugin is `<courseId>:<slug>`, so the layout would leave the
runtime able to read and unable to write. The same applies to course ids, which
come from the learner's own words and are frequently not ASCII.

dsh-diagnostic-tutor README · Why not `per-record`：Making the ids path-safe means a referential migration across courses, nodes,
lessons, focus and decisions, plus changing the ids the tutor passes back to the
tools. That is worth doing deliberately — not as a side effect of flipping a
layout flag. Until then, `single` is the honest choice, and its limit is the one
stated above.
